title: Families of USS Abraham Lincoln Crew Say Trump Should Be 'Ashamed' of Shipboard Conditions
detail: As the USS Abraham Lincoln neared nine months at sea — its fifth consecutive month of combat operations against Iran — families of sailors and Marines aboard went public on August 15, 2026 with reports of intermittent food shortages, low hygiene supplies, plumbing and hot-water failures, and declining mental health, with some unconfirmed reports of sailors attempting to jump overboard. Trump dismissed the concerns, calling the deployment 'not nearly long enough,' comments families called out as dismissive; one relative said 'they can't even get help from him or his administration.' Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said the mission was extended because the Iran conflict demanded it and that mental health cases were treated and meal plans adjusted during shortages; Navy officials meeting with families acknowledged toilet problems aboard the carrier.

media.caption: Families of USS Abraham Lincoln sailors say Trump should be 'ashamed' of conditions on board during the carrier's extended deployment
